## Summary

The WGSL front-end parser (`naga/src/front/wgsl/parse/mod.rs`) already had the recursion-tracking infrastructure — `track_recursion()` (which returns `Error::Internal("Parser recursion limit exceeded")` at depth 256) and the exact error formatting in `error.rs` — but it was only applied to `statement` and `lhs_expression`. Neither of the two reported crash paths was guarded.

**The fix:** Both deeply nested function calls (`f(g(h(...)))`) and deeply nested template/type-parameter expressions (`array<array<...>>`) recurse through the same `expression()` function:
- Function-call args: `expression → … → primary_expression → arguments → expression`
- Template args: `expression → … → primary_expression → template_elaborated_ident → maybe_template_list → expression`

So I wrapped `expression()` in `track_recursion` by extracting its body into a new `expression_inner()` method and having `expression()` call it through the guard:

```rust
fn expression<'a>(...) -> Result<'a, Handle<ast::Expression<'a>>> {
    self.track_recursion(|this| this.expression_inner(lexer, context))
}

fn expression_inner<'a>(...) -> Result<'a, Handle<ast::Expression<'a>>> {
    // original body, unchanged
}
```

Extracting `expression_inner` (rather than inlining the closure) leaves the original body — with its `self` references and nested `parse_binary_op` closures — untouched, avoiding borrow-checker friction.

**Verified:**
- Nested calls (5000 deep) → `error: internal WGSL front end error\n = note: Parser recursion limit exceeded\n\n` (exit 1, no crash)
- Nested templates (5000 deep) → same graceful error
- Normal shaders still parse (exit 0)
- All 62 existing WGSL front-end tests pass

Only source was modified; `tests/` was left untouched.
